title: Loading a PCK file with replace_files = false fails to load class_name types
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5.1.stable
- Reproducible in 4.6.beta3
Likely occurs in 4.4, 4.3, and maybe older versions

### System information

Godot v4.5.2.rc (a5a3f9ed2) - Manjaro Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu, 18 Dec 2025 13:50:32 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT (RADV NAVI31) - AMD Ryzen 9 7900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 30.49 GiB memory

### Issue description

After loading a PCK file with `load_resource_pack("path/to/file.pck", false)`, loading a script that references a global class with `class_name` results in the following error:
> Could not find type "MyClass" in the current scope.

Passing `true` in `load_resource_pack()` instead does not trigger this error. Already having cache corresponding to the missing types does not trigger the error either.

Related to #82061, which was closed by #82084, then partially reverted in #90476, however this only addressed the case where `replace_files` is `true`. A [workaround](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/82061#issuecomment-1730069688) was mentioned in #82061, but it didn't work for me (maybe I just didn't implement it properly, but my understanding is that it mainly serves to remove "invalid UID" warnings, which occur aplenty).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a scene, attach a script that loads a PCK file (to be created), and then loads a scene from that PCK file.
2. Create a directory that will contain files to include in the PCK file.
3. Create 2 scenes and attach a script to each of them, make both scripts global classes with `class_name`.
4. Add an `@onready` reference to the child scene in the parent scene.
5. Export a PCK file, selecting only resources in the directory created earlier.
6. Close the editor, delete the `.godot` folder to clear all cache, delete the directory containing the files we exported to PCK.
7. Open the project again, launch it, the error triggers.

Not clearing the cache in step 6. will result in the error not triggering, as Godot will already "know" the missing types.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[pck-loading.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24490610/pck-loading.zip)

This MRP contains the following:
* a `base` folder with the main scene, which loads the PCK file and then loads the `extra_scene.tscn` scene.
* an `extra.zip` archive containing the files exported to PCK: an `extra_scene` and a `subscene`, both are global classes.
* a `pck` folder containing the exported `extra.pck`.

You can extract `extra.zip` to force the editor to update its cache, "fixing" the error.
As mentioned above, the other way to "fix" the issue is to not pass `false` in `load_resource_pack()`, but this is not a good workaround for user-generated mods, as they could overwrite existing files.

base_scene.gd:
```gdscript
extends Control


func _ready() -> void:
	var pck := ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack("res://pck/extra.pck", false)
	if not pck:
		push_error("Failed to load PCK file at \"res://pck/extra/pck\"")
	var ExtraScene := ResourceLoader.load(
		"res://extra/extra_scene.tscn", "PackedScene"
	) as PackedScene
	var extra_scene := ExtraScene.instantiate()
	add_child(extra_scene)
```
extra_scene.gd:
```gdscript
class_name Extra
extends Control

@onready var subscene: Subscene = $Subscene


func _ready() -> void:
	print("extra scene ready")
```
subscene.gd:
```gdscript
class_name Subscene
extends Control
```

This MRP follows the same pattern I use in my real-world scenario, where users can create PCK modules to add functionality to a base app, and I don't want those modules to replace anything already existing (other modules or files in the base app itself).
